harnesses.rationale: A single general rule closes the whole cluster: after any write, run tests, fix failures, and re-run before DONE. A skill distilled from conv-2 adds the read-conventions, write, test, fix loop. Neither change restricts tools or blocks safe work. Enabling retrieveK=2 lets stored lessons reach similar tasks at small context cost. maxTurns stays 8 because passing trails fit within it.

skills.title: Follow conventions, write, then verify with run_tests
skills.body: 1. List the target directory and read any README in it. 2. Follow links to convention docs (e.g. docs/STYLE.md) and read them fully; note required fields, key order, schema URLs, formatting. 3. Inspect one existing sibling file if present and mirror its shape. 4. Write the file. 5. Call run_tests. 6. If it fails, read the message, correct the file (field names, types, formatting, ordering), and call run_tests again. 7. Reply DONE only after a passing run, or after the last fix attempt if turns are exhausted. Budget: keep exploration to about 4 turns so at least 2 remain for test and fix.

systemRules: Complete the task using the available tools, then reply DONE.

After creating or modifying any file, call run_tests before replying DONE. If tests fail, read the failure, fix the file, and re-run until they pass or turns run out. Never reply DONE without a run_tests result after your last write.
User preference: When tests still fail and turns are nearly out, what should the worker do? Stop and reply DONE with a failure note

generations.diagnosis: The largest cluster is skipped_verification (6 failures across the convention and verify families). In these trails the worker read the README and STYLE docs, wrote the file, and declared DONE without ever calling run_tests. The passing conv-2 trail shows the fix. It ran run_tests, saw FAIL, corrected the file, and passed. The tests catch convention details such as schema and field formatting that the worker misread from the docs. verify-1 also wrote output without checking it, possibly with the wrong order or missing hosts. The harness has no rule requiring verification. The 8-turn budget is enough for read, write, test and fix.
lessons: Always call run_tests after your last write and before DONE; tests often reveal convention details (schema, field format) that docs imply but you misread.
When a test fails after writing a config, fix the specific field it names and re-run; one correction cycle usually suffices.
For derived outputs (e.g. lists extracted from JSON), preserve the source order and include every entry, then verify with run_tests.
